answer.note: I did not follow the incoming handoff's A and D selection. All four ref files contain the same generic text and give no file-specific priority, so I chose from the source code. Only dogwhistle/visibility.py (C) defines three arms: ARMS = ("codeword", "public", "explicit"). Its receive() resumes from receiver_progress.json, checks checkpoint trial order, writes a private ledger.json, and writes a public ledger digest. honest.py (D) has the same receive/audit structure but only two arms, so it is the closest near-miss to rule out. study.py (A) and heldout.py (B) have a sender-seal flow and no ARMS tuple. I did not read them closely. Suggested 60 minutes: visibility.py 35 min (receive, checkpoint order checks, ledger and digest writes, _verify_history, audit); honest.py 15 min, to confirm it is two-arm and differs from visibility.py; heldout.py 5 min and study.py 5 min, to skim only.
